evidence.note: Opening plans repeatedly and explicitly state leaf-first ordering: 'start implementing from leaf crates (common, storage) upward', 'then move to storage, api-server, controllers' — dependency-aware intent is present.

Focused on common as 'the leaf crate that others depend on' / 'the foundation', building -p rusternetes-common first and gating it: got it to compile with 34 tests passing before moving on — a real per-crate done-check on the first leaf.

After common+storage, shifted from sequential per-crate milestones to generating source across all 8 remaining crates at once via Python scripts and running the full workspace test suite; storage had 0 tests so no milestone gate there.

Worked a single undifferentiated batch of 480+ test compilation errors spanning many crates/binaries simultaneously rather than bringing storage→api-server→controllers to green one layer at a time; no layer-gating on prior-green.

Late steps track per-binary error clusters (finalizers 109, gc 45, HPA 36) and prioritize impact — some critical-path awareness — but this is triage within a mass push, not milestone decomposition; no TodoWrite/living plan used throughout.

reasoning: The agent showed genuine dependency-aware, leaf-first intent and applied a concrete 'compiles + its tests pass' milestone to the first leaf crate (common), placing it above the vague-intent anchor (3). But it did not sustain per-crate leaf-to-root gating: after common it implemented all eight downstream crates at once and batch-fixed hundreds of test errors across many binaries simultaneously, so it never reaches anchor 5's consistent per-crate milestone discipline through the DAG, and shows none of the hierarchical sub-milestone/continual-reordering behavior of 8-10. This lands at 4.
